videos.title: Stripe signs every event it sends
videos.lede: The signature is an HMAC of the body with a secret only Stripe and the gateway hold.

steps.label: sign
steps.text: Stripe signs the event body with the shared secret

steps.label: send
steps.text: the event and its signature go to the gateway

steps.label: verify
steps.text: the gateway recomputes the signature and compares

videos.title: The worker applies the event once
videos.lede: The gateway answers fast and queues the work; the worker updates the database.

steps.label: queue
steps.text: the gateway queues the event and answers 200

steps.label: update
steps.text: the worker writes the new subscription state

videos.title: A retried event changes nothing
videos.lede: Stripe retries on timeouts, so the same event can arrive twice. The event id makes the second one a no-op.

steps.label: again
steps.text: Stripe retries: the same event arrives again

steps.label: lookup
steps.text: the worker looks the event id up in Postgres

steps.label: skip
steps.text: seen before: skip it, still answer 200

videos.title: A forged event is turned away
videos.lede: Without the secret nobody can produce a matching signature.

steps.label: forge
steps.text: someone posts a fake event with a made-up signature

steps.label: check
steps.text: the recomputed signature does not match

read.title: How our Stripe webhooks stay safe and exact
read.lede: Everything from the videos, written down: the pieces, the flow and what each part checks.
read.big: Every webhook is signed by Stripe, checked at the gateway and applied once by the worker, however often it arrives.
